scenes.title: The last wind
scenes.objective: Preserve the sound of home before departure.

tasks.title: Wind screen
tasks.prompt: Knocks vanish when the Archivist shelters the microphone with her hand. The distant towers are still audible. What can she leave in place when she lets go?
options: Set the recorder on a folded cloth
tasks.note: Shielded the microphone against wind noise.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: What changed when she used her hand?
Air hitting the capsule and vibration travelling up the stand have different remedies.
Choose “Fit the felt sleeve”. Shielded the microphone against wind noise.

tasks.title: Recording levels
tasks.prompt: The meter reaches the red mark on every gust. The quiet passages are still audible.
options: Lower the gain until peaks stay below red
tasks.note: Set recording headroom.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.

puzzle.instruction: Set the recorder without clipping. The gust is 6 dB louder than the current peak at -3 dB. Make the smallest gain change that leaves at least 3 dB of headroom.

hints: Start by working out where the louder gust would peak at the current setting.
The next peak would be +3 dB. Count how far it must move to reach -3 dB.
Choose -6 dB. A bigger reduction also avoids clipping, but loses more level than necessary.

tasks.title: Departure recorder
tasks.prompt: The departure has three sounds in order: the tower wind, an engine lifting, then a silence where the engine was. What would preserve their timing for someone who never heard them?
options: Make a separate reel for each sound
Stop the tape during the quiet passage
tasks.note: Preserved the wind on Veyr.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Consider what a listener can learn from the silence.
A splice can preserve the order of events while losing their spacing.
Choose “Record the whole passage”. Preserved the wind on Veyr.

shots.direction: Track upward through glass towers to a dying red sun and departing lights.

tasks.title: Interpreter’s notebook
tasks.prompt: The delegate says “compare our demonstrations.” One interpreter’s draft uses “prove”; another adds “which was stronger.” Helen needs to translate the proposal without adding a claim.
options: You propose a test of which field was stronger
You propose discussing what was demonstrated
You propose proving the apparatus can work
tasks.note: Kept the translation neutral.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Listen for the verb the delegate actually used.
Comparing observations leaves their explanation open. Ranking or proving them adds a promise.
Choose “You propose discussing what was demonstrated”. Kept the translation neutral.

tasks.title: Joint statement
tasks.prompt: The interpreters have two records to fill. Helen must leave each delegate room to speak for their own team.
options: Ask both delegates about their own apparatus
Record a shared conclusion about the mechanism
tasks.note: Both Meridian demonstrations were staged.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.

puzzle.instruction: The American observer saw a ring on the Chinese screen. The Chinese observer saw a ring on the American screen. Neither inspected the other room. Each engineering team brought its own projection diagram. The joint minutes are public; the diagrams were offered in the closed session.

rows.label: Question for both delegates
options: What produced the ring in your room?
How did the other team produce its ring?
How far did the other team move the target?

rows.label: Entry in the joint minutes
options: Two projectors, one in each room
Both targets moved the same distance

hints: Separate what an observer saw from what an engineer did.
Each delegate can explain one apparatus in private. Both can attest to one visible feature in public.
Ask what produced the ring in each delegate’s own room. Record only that both observers saw a ring in the joint minutes.

tasks.title: Private record
tasks.prompt: The two delegates approve the same public sentence. Helen also heard each private admission. What belongs in the notebook she keeps for herself?
options: Separately attributed remarks and the final agreement
A single admission credited to both delegates
tasks.note: Helen preserved the truth in Mandarin shorthand.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: The notebook may be read years after the speakers are gone.
A reader should be able to distinguish who spoke in private from what both signed.
Choose “Separately attributed remarks and the final agreement”. Helen preserved the truth in Mandarin shorthand.

shots.direction: Push across an empty conference table toward a notebook, then the pulse outside.

scenes.title: The bay is singing
scenes.objective: Find the hum beneath the radio static.

tasks.title: Frank’s radio
tasks.prompt: A low musical hum sits between two loud stations. Narrow the receiver bandwidth.
options: Tune between the stations and narrow the band
tasks.note: Found the ship’s hum beneath the radio static.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Move the dial between the two clear broadcasts and listen for a third sound.
The hum is near 815 kHz. A broad setting still lets the adjacent stations through.
Set 815 kHz, choose the narrow bandwidth, then record.

tasks.title: Phone and notebook
tasks.prompt: Frank needs both hands on the set. Helen has a dry notebook in the boat. Steve’s recorded greeting ends with a beep. Which record could Steve find at home tonight?
options: Write a second copy in the boat log
Call the Thursday club from Frank’s receiver
tasks.note: Helen called Steve before the boat disappeared.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Where will each record be when the boat leaves?
Steve can retrieve something left on his own phone.
Choose “Leave Steve a message”. Helen called Steve before the boat disappeared.

shots.direction: Drift beside the rowboat as turquoise light grows beneath black water.

scenes.title: Good Morning, Sleepyhead
scenes.objective: Find out whether the repeated greeting is a fault in the recorder.

tasks.title: Saturday take
tasks.prompt: The leader reads SAT. A loose work reel holds an earlier kitchen test. Steve wants evidence he can date without relying on memory.
options: Copy both takes onto the work reel without markers
Use the kitchen test as the Saturday reference
tasks.note: Preserved Saturday’s greeting.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: The date has to stay attached to the sound.
An earlier recording from the same room does not establish what Steve heard on Saturday.
Choose “Keep the original recording”. Preserved Saturday’s greeting.

tasks.title: Sunday take
tasks.prompt: On Sunday Steve can set the recorder running before Nora comes in. How could he compare an ordinary morning with Saturday without teaching her the rhythm he remembers?
options: Play Saturday first and ask for another greeting
Record the greeting without prompting her
Say the greeting first and ask her to reply
tasks.note: Preserved Sunday’s greeting.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Keep the conditions of the two mornings as similar as possible.
A demonstration or a verbal cue can change the second performance.
Choose “Record the greeting without prompting her”. Preserved Sunday’s greeting.

tasks.title: Recorder control test
tasks.prompt: Steve tests a different stretch of tape. He hears “one, two” twice. A chair squeaks between the words only on the second pass. Which claim has this test actually challenged?
options: Nora used the same words twice
The transport loops the last input on every pass
tasks.note: Ruled out a stuck or looping recorder.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Use the squeak as a marker independent of the words.
A transport that always replayed the earlier pass would replay the earlier room noise too.
Choose “The transport loops the last input on every pass”. Ruled out a stuck or looping recorder.

tasks.title: Compare greetings
tasks.prompt: Listen to Saturday and Sunday. Compare the breath, onset and pause, not just the words.
options: Similar delivery with a new breath
tasks.note: Two independently captured greetings are the same take.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.

puzzle.instruction: Line up the breath and first word, then compare the small peaks and pauses throughout both recordings.
hints: Line up the quiet breath and first word. Then look along the rest of both waveforms.
Sunday starts later than Saturday. Move Sunday to the left; compare pauses as well as large peaks.
Move Sunday 0.35 seconds earlier (-0.35 s). Choose Identical performance.

shots.direction: Move from a dark reel-to-reel recorder toward amber kitchen light.

scenes.title: Sunday on the pier
scenes.objective: Look for independent evidence around town.

tasks.title: Admiral’s pool
tasks.prompt: Admiral took Steve’s lunch. Nora whistles while Admiral is underwater; the harbor winch is running. He keeps swimming. What should go in the observation column?
options: He failed to turn during this whistle
He heard Nora and chose to ignore her
Nora’s second note was too low
tasks.note: Admiral ignored the apparent Nora’s whistle.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Separate what Steve saw from what he thinks Admiral heard.
The winch and the water leave more than one explanation.
Choose “He failed to turn during this whistle”. Admiral ignored the apparent Nora’s whistle.

tasks.title: Deputy Lyle
tasks.prompt: Lyle holds a door and remembers the boys’ birthday. Steve remembers him as a colder man. What independent follow-up would help date the change?
options: Ask when he first began coming to their games
Test whether he remembers Steve’s old address
tasks.note: Lyle’s behavior changed; behavior alone proves nothing.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Steve needs a date for the new habit.
Old memories can establish familiarity without dating a change in behavior.
Choose “Ask when he first began coming to their games”. Lyle’s behavior changed; behavior alone proves nothing.

tasks.title: Penhallow’s bait stall
tasks.prompt: Penhallow hums along to a low note. Her lips go still before the note dies away across the water. Steve wants to learn where it comes from.
options: Ask which part of the bay she hears it from
Ask when she learned the melody
Ask whether she hums it in the shop
tasks.note: Penhallow knows about the bay’s recurring tone.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Separate Agnes’s breath from the sound she follows.
The note brackets the humming. June and the winch operator each rule out a different explanation.
Place the start of the water note first and its end last. File the water as the possible source, Agnes as the imitation, the winch as the early stop and June as the independent ear.

puzzle.instruction: Agnes has been keeping a tide book in a bait tin. Help her work out which sound she was humming along to.
evidence: Agnes marked the first low note with a dot, the start of her humming with a loop, her last breath with a cross, and the end of the low note with a bar.
On the damp page the dot is two squares before the loop. The cross immediately precedes the bar. She wrote on one square at a time, left to right.

June stood upwind at the fish shed. She heard the low note before Agnes started, but could never hear Agnes herself. With the winch stopped she heard it most clearly beside the water under the floating dock.
Agnes left three pockets in the tin for a possible source, an imitation, and a noise that stopped too soon. The winch operator says he stopped halfway through the low note.

stages.prompt: Reconstruct the four pencil marks in the order Agnes made them. Empty squares can lie between marks.
File the sound and witness cards by what June and the winch operator actually establish.

hints: Separate Agnes’s breath from the sound she follows.
The note brackets the humming. June and the winch operator each rule out a different explanation.
Place the start of the water note first and its end last. File the water as the possible source, Agnes as the imitation, the winch as the early stop and June as the independent ear.

shots.direction: Follow Steve along the pier, then join the Reyes family at La Marea for Sunday dinner.

scenes.title: A plate kept warm
scenes.objective: Listen to Nora’s family before drawing a conclusion.

tasks.title: Carmen’s birthday
tasks.prompt: Mateo drove Nora to the restaurant; Rafa took her home. Carmen remembers the meal but spent most of it in the kitchen. Which entries could later establish how long Nora stayed?
options: Mateo’s arrival and Rafa’s departure times
Carmen’s menu and the restaurant hours
Nora’s shift roster and the table booking
tasks.note: Nora had a documented alibi on Carmen’s birthday.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Which family members actually witnessed the endpoints?
A booking describes a plan; a ride places someone at the restaurant.
Choose “Mateo’s arrival and Rafa’s departure times”. Nora had a documented alibi on Carmen’s birthday.

tasks.title: Tomás’s recorder
tasks.prompt: Tomás has three years of field reels. His published episodes splice sounds from several nights. What should Steve borrow to investigate the dates?
options: The episodes arranged by broadcast date
The field reels with their original labels
An undated compilation of the clearest hums
tasks.note: Tomás retained dated bay recordings.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Start with the day the buoy was ashore.
The repaired buoy accounts for the two knocks. The pencil log ties those sounds to the spindles.
The nights begin with one bell, a gull and two knocks. Pack Salt, Thread and Glass, then the red copy.

puzzle.instruction: Tomás will lend Steve the field reels if he can put the borrowed tapes back on the right spindles. The published episode has three cuts in it.
evidence: From Tomás’s log. On the 3rd, low tide exposed the bell buoy. On the 12th the buoy was ashore, with a cracked clapper. On the 21st the repair crew gave it a double tap before launching.
Natural starts, as logged in pencil: one bell on Salt, a gull on Thread, two uneven knocks on Glass. On the red broadcast copy Tomás spliced Glass into Salt, then Salt into Thread.
The milk crate has four pockets in listening order. Borrow the three uncut nights in date order. File the edited copy last, with its paper edit list.

stages.prompt: Put an opening sound beside each field date. Use the repair history to identify the silent buoy.
Pack the crate so Steve can check the original intervals before he listens to the broadcast.

hints: Start with the day the buoy was ashore.
The repaired buoy accounts for the two knocks. The pencil log ties those sounds to the spindles.
The nights begin with one bell, a gull and two knocks. Pack Salt, Thread and Glass, then the red copy.

tasks.title: Nora at dinner
tasks.prompt: Nora now agrees with Carmen about a recipe she used to argue over. Carmen notices too. Which conclusion can Steve support tonight?
options: Nora has forgotten how the dish used to taste
Two witnesses noticed a change worth following
They know when and why Nora changed her mind
tasks.note: Several people noticed Nora’s changed behavior.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Count the observations, then consider what caused them.
Agreement between two witnesses about a change does not date it or explain it.
Choose “Two witnesses noticed a change worth following”. Several people noticed Nora’s changed behavior.

shots.direction: Settle beside the family table, with harbor lights through rain-streaked glass.

scenes.title: The ninth night
scenes.objective: Check the work order and leave the locked apartment.

tasks.title: Coat pocket
tasks.prompt: The north-wing work order has a handwritten sign-off at 20:15 on Carmen’s birthday. Mateo brought Nora to dinner at noon; Rafa took her home at midnight. Which discrepancy should Steve check first?
options: The sign-off against the family’s witnessed interval
The form’s print date against the reservation date
The work-order number against the menu price
tasks.note: The aquarium work order contradicts a witnessed alibi.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Correct each clock in the opposite direction from its error.
The corrected kitchen and north-wing times coincide. Which source shows a face, and which shows a name?
Parking was noon. Both evening slips mean 20:15. Use Mateo, Carmen’s photo, the work order and Rafa. The earliest round trip would require Nora to be gone from 19:57 to 20:33.

puzzle.instruction: Rain has stuck the aquarium paperwork to the lining of a coat. Steve has three independent clocks and one apparent signature.
evidence: Control card: the aquarium wall clock ran 15 minutes fast all day. The kitchen clock at La Marea agreed with harbor time. The parking machine ran 10 minutes slow.
Printed slips: parking 11:50, north-wing sign-off 20:30, kitchen birthday check 20:15. Rafa wrote midnight in his own hand when he drove Nora home.
Mateo drove Nora directly from the parking machine to the restaurant at noon. Carmen's kitchen photograph shows Nora holding the birthday check inside La Marea. The aquarium is across the bay.
Rafa can attest to the ride home. Only the signed work order puts someone using Nora’s name inside the north wing.

The quickest crossing took 18 minutes each way. On Carmen’s contact strip two restaurant pictures also show Nora at 20:04 and 20:29. Use the corrected aquarium time to mark the narrowest possible absence.

stages.prompt: Correct the three machine times. Two events share a time; use the place as well as the clock.
Attach a source to each part of the discrepancy. Keep the signature separate from an eyewitness.
Build the shortest round trip that could cover a 20:15 signature. Place the two pictures inside its limits.

hints: Correct each clock in the opposite direction from its error.
The corrected kitchen and north-wing times coincide. Which source shows a face, and which shows a name?
Parking was noon. Both evening slips mean 20:15. Use Mateo, Carmen’s photo, the work order and Rafa. The earliest round trip would require Nora to be gone from 19:57 to 20:33.

tasks.title: Balcony wiring
tasks.prompt: The neighbor is halfway down the stairs and cannot see the last turn. Steve must open the balcony gate while the stair bulb stays lit from start to finish. The service selector has three positions.
options: Cycle the light and motor together
Queue the release and restart the motor with the stair lit
Try the thumb pad with the motor running
tasks.note: Released the neighbor’s balcony latch.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.

puzzle.instruction: NORMAL feeds the stair bulb and latch motor. SERVICE feeds the bulb alone. OFF feeds neither. A thumb pad can store a release request only while the motor is idle. The return spring clears the request the instant the pad rises. The motor checks for a stored request only when it starts.

rows.label: While the pad is still in that position

hints: Track the stair bulb separately from the latch motor.
The request must survive until the motor starts. Which position lets you store one without darkening the stairs?
Choose SERVICE, press and keep pressure, then switch to NORMAL.

tasks.title: Iris pots
tasks.prompt: The pots lean against the inner rail. The landing door needs a key from the stair side. Through the neighbor’s open balcony gate Steve can see the illuminated communal stair.
options: Follow the shared rail to the communal stair
Pull the landing door shut and try its outside handle
Pass the stair and try the unlit fire door
tasks.note: Escaped while the apparent Nora hesitated.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Use only a route Steve can see is open.
The landing handle is on the wrong side.
Choose “Follow the shared rail to the communal stair”. Escaped while the apparent Nora hesitated.

shots.direction: Follow the balcony escape, then reveal a procession entering luminous surf.

scenes.title: The Aquarium Is Closed
scenes.objective: Follow the old exhibit plan to the sealed wing.

tasks.title: Exhibit plan
tasks.prompt: The old plan and a newer maintenance notice disagree. Steve needs a route into the north wing.
options: Reach the outgoing pump route from the service entrance
Trace an incoming pipe back toward the pump
tasks.note: Located the north-wing service route.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.

puzzle.instruction: On the plan the café and public tank both feed the visitor hall. The service door feeds the pump room. The visitor hall leads to the north wing through door 1. Notice: door 1 was bricked up; the pump room has three pipes now. Flow arrows point from N into the pump, from the pump into E, and from S into the pump. The maintenance slip says to follow the only pipe carrying water away from the pump.

hints: Use the newer notice when two documents conflict.
The old visitor route depends on door 1. At the pump compare both ends of the flow arrows.
Use the service door and follow E, the only outgoing pipe.

tasks.title: Two service doors
tasks.prompt: Steve records six seconds at each door. Which passage can he cross without meeting the guard?
options: Wait for both doors to go silent
tasks.note: Distinguished an announcement loop from a live guard.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Look for a sound that repeats at the same interval.
Compare the spacing and shapes of the peaks in each six-second strip.
Take the filter corridor. The bell and cough repeat together there; the footsteps at the pump change their spacing.

tasks.title: Nora’s coat and intercom
tasks.prompt: The spool starts before Nora states her name. A date mark remains on the leader, and two notes follow the speech. What would let somebody else check both her identity and the date later?
options: File the intact spool and its marked leader
Keep the two notes alone with a new date label
Copy the name only and discard the leader
tasks.note: Recovered Nora’s intercom tape and whistle.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Start with the pencilled star rather than a sound.
Follow the splice into the blue line. The two versions of the whistle differ in what is still attached.
The order is dated leader, clear tape, voice, whistle. The loose duplicate belongs in the unverified pocket.

puzzle.instruction: A paper leader has come loose from Nora’s intercom spool. Steve can preserve the whole recording before he makes a listening copy.
evidence: On the leader Nora wrote the date and drew half a star across its splice. The matching half is on clear tape. At the other end of the clear tape someone drew a blue line before speaking.
Steve hears Nora name herself after the blue line and before the two whistle notes. A loose duplicate contains the notes only.
The evidence drawer has separate pockets for when, who, what Admiral might recognize, and a copy without a date. Keep the original attached from leader to whistle.

stages.prompt: Lay the original strip out from its dated head to its audible tail.
Label the evidence pockets so a second listener could verify each claim.

hints: Start with the pencilled star rather than a sound.
Follow the splice into the blue line. The two versions of the whistle differ in what is still attached.
The order is dated leader, clear tape, voice, whistle. The loose duplicate belongs in the unverified pocket.

shots.direction: Pass dark empty exhibits into an amber transit chamber beneath new plywood.

scenes.title: Sixty-one percent
scenes.objective: Record a command and interrupt the scan.

tasks.title: Amber sleeper
tasks.prompt: At the bed, Nora’s chest rises irregularly against the glass. A pulse travels down the corridor at even intervals. Steve wants to check for a response without disturbing life support.
options: Speak close to the bed and watch her breathing
Use the corridor pulse as Nora’s breathing rate
Use the brightness of the next bed as her pulse
tasks.note: Confirmed that the real Nora is alive.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: Look for the one rhythm that loses a beat against the ship.
Only the mouth patch has unequal gaps. Steve can show a hand through glass while keeping the rail still.
The corridor, rail and mouth are A, B and C. Log the resting rhythm, raise a hand, mark the next patch, then compare the corridor.

puzzle.instruction: Behind the amber glass, one rhythm belongs to the ship. Steve wants to find out whether Nora is breathing without touching her life support.
evidence: Steve marked the corridor flash at seconds 2, 6 and 10. The pickup on the rail repeated each flash one second later. A fog patch above Nora’s mouth appeared at 3, 7 and 12.
Three rubbings lost their labels. Strip A reads 2 / 6 / 10, strip B reads 3 / 7 / 11, and strip C reads 3 / 7 / 12. Steve used the same stopwatch throughout.
The observation card separates a timing reference, a second reading of the ship cycle, and evidence consistent with breathing. Steve can make one further observation through sealed glass.

A reliable comparison needs an undisturbed mouth reading. Steve can signal with an upraised hand but must note the first breath afterwards before checking the corridor marks. Touching the rail would disturb the ship pickup.

stages.prompt: Recover the labels on the rubbings by comparing the marks with the notes.
Plan the independent observation while keeping the sleeper sealed.
pieces: Raise Steve’s hand at the glass

rows.label: Before the cue
options: Raise Steve’s hand at the glass

rows.label: Give a cue
options: Raise Steve’s hand at the glass

rows.label: Watch the next breath
options: Raise Steve’s hand at the glass

rows.label: Check the reference
options: Raise Steve’s hand at the glass

hints: Look for the one rhythm that loses a beat against the ship.
Only the mouth patch has unequal gaps. Steve can show a hand through glass while keeping the rail still.
The corridor, rail and mouth are A, B and C. Log the resting rhythm, raise a hand, mark the next patch, then compare the corridor.

tasks.title: Saren’s intercom
tasks.prompt: An attendant asks the chair to open. Nothing happens. Saren answers over the intercom and the buckle releases during his last words. What should Steve mark on the reel?
options: Saren’s reply from first word to last
The attendant’s request before the reply
Only the noise of the buckle opening
tasks.note: Recorded Saren’s restraint-release command.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.
hints: The lamp and buckle respond during the second voice.
A name or sentence alone would omit the response. Preserve the channel opening too.

Place attendant, Saren, buckle and bare leader on the strip. For the working copy use silence, the complete command and the click, then file the blank tail separately. Ash is the failed request, Elm the spoken release, Reed the manual test.

puzzle.instruction: Steve finds two voices and a relay click on the chair circuit. The attendant’s words sound convincing. On his reel there is also a relay click.
evidence: Tape edge, left to right: a large splice, one short mark, two short marks, then bare leader. Through headphones Steve hears the attendant before the first mark and Saren between the two marked groups.
The maintenance lamp stays dark for the attendant. It lights during Saren’s words. Steve marked the buckle click in the two-mark group, before the bare leader.
For a working copy, start with enough silence to hear the channel open, keep Saren’s complete words, and leave the buckle click in place. Return the blank tail to its own envelope.

Three short carbon traces came away with the relay log. Ash shows speech with the lamp dark. Elm has authorized speech and an open buckle. Reed has an open buckle after someone pressed a separate manual test switch.

stages.prompt: Place the events on the strip. Use the edge marks to distinguish the two voices.
Lay out the verification copy, followed by the part returned to its envelope.
Use the test traces to separate what the two voices demonstrate from what the chair can do by itself.

hints: The lamp and buckle respond during the second voice.
A name or sentence alone would omit the response. Preserve the channel opening too.

Place attendant, Saren, buckle and bare leader on the strip. For the working copy use silence, the complete command and the click, then file the blank tail separately. Ash is the failed request, Elm the spoken release, Reed the manual test.

tasks.title: Scan chair
tasks.prompt: The scan is moving again. Steve has three recordings on Frank’s reel and can reach two microphone grilles.
options: Route the clip to the Gallery speakers
Deliver the captured service phrase during the long scan window
tasks.note: Interrupted the scan at 61% and escaped through the flooded intake.
tasks.hint: Look at the evidence in the description, then try another approach.

puzzle.instruction: The attendant spoke into the grille with the broken rim when testing the gallery speakers. The undamaged grille made the chair’s service lamp blink. The lamp stays lit for one second on an ordinary scan beat and for six seconds at the notch marked 61. The chair listens only while the lamp is lit and drops an unfinished phrase when it goes dark.

hints: Preview the three cues. Which speaker has already been obeyed by this chair?
Separate the public speakers from the local service input. The complete authorization lasts longer than one ordinary beat.
Choose cue 03, the undamaged grille, and the start of the 61 notch.

shots.direction: Reveal the Gallery, close on the scan meter, then follow light into the flooding intake.

p_veyr.in.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.in.01.text: There are forty thousand names on the departure register. I have checked every one.

p_veyr.out.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.out.01.text: Wind through the western towers. Last evening. Original take.

p_veyr.out.02.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.out.02.text: I will remember where we lived.

p_veyr.shield.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.shield.01.text: Now I can hear the city, beneath the wind.

p_veyr.levels.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.levels.01.text: Leave room for the loud parts. They belong to the record too.

p_meeting.in.01.speaker: general_us
p_meeting.in.01.text: We are prepared to discuss the practical status of our demonstration.

p_meeting.in.02.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.in.02.text: After you explain the difference between practical and actual.

p_meeting.out.01.speaker: helen
p_meeting.out.01.text: Everyone agreed to keep lying. It may be the most honest thing I have seen.

p_meeting.terms.01.speaker: helen
p_meeting.terms.01.text: They propose that both teams describe what the observers actually saw.

p_meeting.terms.02.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.terms.02.text: That would be a useful place to begin.

p_meeting.confess.02.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.confess.02.text: There was no engine at our test either.

p_meeting.confess.03.speaker: helen
p_meeting.confess.03.text: Then we can discuss what to do next.

p_meeting.record.01.speaker: helen
p_meeting.record.01.text: Dates. Names. What each person actually said. Someone may need the truth one day.

p_bay.in.01.speaker: frank
p_bay.in.01.text: Same interval as last Thursday. Louder out here.

p_bay.in.02.speaker: helen
p_bay.in.02.text: Steve is working. I’ll leave him a message.

p_bay.out.01.speaker: helen
p_bay.out.01.text: Come out with us, kiddo. The bay is singing tonight.

p_bay.tune.01.speaker: frank
p_bay.tune.01.text: There you are. I can hear more than one voice.

p_bay.message.01.speaker: helen
p_bay.message.01.text: He should hear this for himself. We’ll bring the tape home.

c1_flat.in.01.speaker: helen
c1_flat.in.01.text: Come out with us, kiddo. The bay is singing tonight.

c1_flat.in.03.speaker: autorick
c1_flat.in.03.text: Good morning, Bellwether! Yesterday will be sunny.

c1_flat.out.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.out.01.text: Same breath. Same tiny click before the second word.

c1_flat.out.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.out.02.text: I need evidence. Being afraid of something doesn’t make it true.

c1_flat.control.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.control.01.text: Testing. One, two. Testing... one, two.

c1_flat.compare.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.01.text: She remembers our first date better than I do. But people don’t do this.

c1_pier.in.02.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.in.02.text: Fish don’t sing, Steven. Something under them does.

c1_pier.out.01.speaker: pell
c1_pier.out.01.text: Your parents’ mail, Mr. Mercer. Delivered precisely on schedule.

c1_pier.out.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.out.02.text: They haven’t been home for eighteen months.

c1_pier.whistle.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.01.text: You always come for that whistle. What’s different today?

c1_pier.door.01.speaker: lyle_copy
c1_pier.door.01.text: They’re both pitching today. I promised I’d watch every inning.

c1_pier.door.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.door.02.text: Lyle remembered a promise. I should probably write that down.

c1_pier.bait.01.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.bait.01.text: Count the nights, Steven. You were always good with numbers when you wrote them down.

c1_dinner.in.01.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.in.01.text: Your plate is warm. Sit. You can apologize while you eat.

c1_dinner.in.02.speaker: rafa
c1_dinner.in.02.text: I kept the sauce separate. You used to like it that way.

c1_dinner.out.01.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.out.01.text: She stopped arguing with me. My daughter has argued with me since she could talk.

c1_dinner.birthday.01.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.birthday.01.text: I drove her here. Rafa drove her home. Midnight, give or take ten minutes.

c1_dinner.podcast.01.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.podcast.01.text: You can borrow them. You could also have listened any time in the last three years.

c1_dinner.family.02.speaker: luis
c1_dinner.family.02.text: Eat before it gets cold, Steve. Then tell us what is troubling you.

c1_escape.in.01.speaker: iris
c1_escape.in.01.text: No. He does not know where the notebook is. Tonight? Understood.

c1_escape.in.02.speaker: steve
c1_escape.in.02.text: Nora? Why is the front door locked?

c1_escape.out.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.out.01.text: She could have stopped me. She stood there and let me go.

c1_escape.order.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.01.text: Noon to midnight at La Marea. Mateo and Rafa both saw her. She couldn’t have signed this there.

c1_escape.power.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.power.01.text: I fixed this for Mr. Bell last winter. For once, something I repaired is useful.

c1_escape.cross.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.cross.01.text: Sorry. Sorry. Those were your irises.

c2_aquarium.in.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.01.text: Emergency. Bellwether Aquarium. Someone is... hello?

c2_aquarium.in.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.02.text: Half a sentence. I hope someone heard it.

c2_aquarium.out.01.speaker: nora
c2_aquarium.out.01.text: My name is Nora Reyes, and somebody just walked out of here wearing my face.

c2_aquarium.out.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.out.02.text: Five months. I didn’t notice for five months.

c2_aquarium.plan.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.01.text: Nora showed me this when I repaired the underwater speakers.

c2_aquarium.guard.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.guard.01.text: The cough was in exactly the same place. That corridor has a recording.

c2_aquarium.intercom.01.speaker: nora
c2_aquarium.intercom.01.text: Two short notes. If Admiral can hear me, perhaps somebody else can.

c2_ship.in.01.speaker: iris
c2_ship.in.01.text: Please come with us. They want to know where your mother put her notebook.

c2_ship.in.02.speaker: guard
c2_ship.in.02.text: Would peaceful human hold music assist your experience?

c2_ship.out.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.out.01.text: The room is flooding. The underwater speakers still work... Nora’s whistle.

c2_ship.nora.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.01.text: I kept waiting until I knew what to say. I’m here now. I should have been here sooner.

sound_labels.effect.veyr_wind: Listen: the last wind on Veyr

greeting.title: Why did I hear the same greeting twice?

theories.text: My recorder is playing a piece of old tape.
I was tired and heard a match that was never there.
Since the boat vanished, I may be reading too much into ordinary things.
Could someone else have used Nora’s name?

aquarium.title: What happened in the north wing?

theories.text: The work order was an ordinary repair with the wrong date.
The woman I heard on that tape might still be here.
